name: Medical
summary: Medicine supply, records, providers, medical orders and the equipment you depend on.
intro: What a household needs in place so that care can continue away from home, without power, or with a different doctor. Ask your own doctor or pharmacist before changing how you take or store any medicine.
groups: Records and who may be told

items.done: Done when each person who takes regular medicine has a current handwritten medication list in the document pouch and in their wallet.
Done when a pharmacy printout of each person's medicines and a copy of every glasses or contact-lens prescription are in the grab bag's document pouch.
Done when each prescriber has said how large an emergency supply you may keep and how early each refill can be collected.
Done when every prescription has the agreed spare supply at home, in its labeled container, rotated oldest first.
Done when each refrigerated medicine has its time-out-of-fridge limit written on the box and a cooler with frozen packs is ready.
Done when one unopened, in-date pack of each basic over-the-counter medicine is stored, and each child's dose for their current weight is written on the medication list.
Done when expired and unused medicines have been taken to a take-back site or disposed of as the FDA advises.

items.title: Ask your pharmacist what emergency refill your state allows
items.done: Done when each person on daily medicine has asked their pharmacist whether, and how much, they could get as an emergency or early refill if the prescriber cannot be reached.

items.title: Fill each regular prescription at the pharmacy you would turn to in an emergency
items.done: Done when every daily, non-controlled prescription has been filled at least once at the pharmacy you would use, since Illinois lets a pharmacist give up to a 30-day emergency supply only for a medicine that pharmacy has filled before.

form.label: Illinois Pharmacy Practice Act, emergency prescription refills (225 ILCS 85/15.3)

items.title: If anyone has no health insurance, learn about the federal emergency prescription program
items.done: Done when anyone without health insurance knows that the Emergency Prescription Assistance Program can replace medicines and supplies when it is switched on for a disaster, and where to find an enrolled pharmacy.

items.group: Records and who may be told
items.done: Done when each person has a dated one-page medical summary in their bag and a copy at home.

items.group: Records and who may be told
items.done: Done when both sides of every health, dental and prescription insurance card are copied and kept with your documents.

items.group: Records and who may be told
items.done: Done when the doctor, pharmacy and any home-care or equipment supplier for each person are on the printed numbers sheet.

items.group: Records and who may be told
items.title: Set up patient-portal access or get copies of each person's key health records
items.done: Done when each adult can sign in to their main providers' patient portals, or has asked for copies of their records, and knows providers normally have up to 30 days to supply them.

items.group: Records and who may be told
items.title: Get a copy of each person's immunization record
items.done: Done when a current immunization record for each person is in the document pouch and checked off on the document checklist.

items.group: Records and who may be told
items.title: Download Illinois immunization records from Vax Verify or request them from I-CARE
items.done: Done when each adult has downloaded their own record from Vax Verify, a legal guardian has added each child under 18 to their own Vax Verify profile and downloaded that record too, or sent the IDPH record request form where that fails, and the records are in the document pouch.

form.label: IDPH I-CARE page: Vax Verify and Authorization to Release Immunization Records

items.group: Records and who may be told
items.title: Request Michigan immunization records from your provider, county or MDHHS
items.done: Done when each person's record has been obtained from their provider, the local county health department or the MDHHS request form, and is in the document pouch.

form.label: MDHHS Division of Immunization: vaccination records

items.group: Records and who may be told
items.title: Tell each doctor and pharmacy who may be told about your care
items.done: Done when each adult has told their doctors and pharmacy which family members or friends may be given information about their care, and signed any form the office uses for this.
Done when every phone in the household shows a medical ID and emergency contacts on the lock screen.
Done when anyone whose condition changes emergency treatment wears or carries medical ID every day.
Done when a dated medical information sheet is posted inside the front door or on the fridge for each person who needs one.
Done when every powered medical device has a tested backup that lasts at least one night and the electricity company knows about it.
Done when each medical device's maker, model, serial number and supplier phone are written on the medical summary.
Done when each clinic, supplier or home-care agency you rely on has told you its emergency plan and its answers are on the medical summary.
Done when two other places that can give any treatment you cannot miss are written on the medical summary.
Done when spare glasses, hearing-aid batteries or chargers and mobility-aid chargers are together in one labeled pouch.

items.title: Find out how to get care when you are away from home
items.done: Done when each adult has their health plan's member-services number on the insurance and legal list and knows an emergency room must screen and stabilize an emergency whatever their insurance.

items.title: Save crisis lines and plan how mental-health care would continue
items.done: Done when 988 and the Disaster Distress Helpline are saved in every phone, and anyone in mental-health or addiction treatment has asked their clinician how care and medicines would continue in an emergency.
Done when each child's fever medicine, the oral syringe that came with it and the dose for their current weight are packed together.
Done when each person or animal who depends on you has a care-instructions sheet that a stranger could follow.
Done when anyone who needs help from responders has a one-page note saying how to help them.
Done when each older or vulnerable relative who lives elsewhere has their own plan and kit.
Done when anyone who could not leave without help has asked about paratransit and assisted evacuation and written down the answers.

items.title: If someone is pregnant, agree on a backup place for prenatal care and birth
items.done: Done when the pregnant person has a plan from their provider for where to get prenatal care or give birth if the usual office or hospital is closed, with their records in the document pouch.

items.title: If anyone has a serious illness, ask their clinician about a portable medical order
items.done: Done when anyone with a serious or life-limiting illness has discussed a portable medical order (such as POLST) with their clinician, and any signed order is kept where emergency crews will find it.

items.title: Complete the Illinois POLST form with a practitioner if it applies
items.done: Done when anyone in Illinois who chooses one has an IDPH Uniform POLST form signed by them or their legal representative and by their practitioner (no witness is needed), kept at home where EMS can find it quickly, with a copy for their legal decision maker.

form.label: IDPH Advance Directives page (Uniform POLST form)

items.title: Complete the Michigan MI-POST form with a clinician if it applies
items.done: Done when anyone in Michigan with a serious advanced illness or frailty who chooses one has an MI-POST signed by them or their representative and their physician, nurse practitioner or physician assistant, the original stays with the person, and a reminder is set to reaffirm it every year and within 30 days of any change the state lists, because an overdue form is void.

form.label: MDHHS MI-POST page (form MDHHS-5836 and information sheet)

items.title: If anyone does not want resuscitation at home, get an out-of-hospital DNR order
items.done: Done when anyone who does not want CPR outside a hospital has a do-not-resuscitate order on their state's form, signed as that form requires and kept where emergency crews will see it.

items.title: In Illinois, record a do-not-resuscitate choice on the IDPH POLST form
items.done: Done when anyone in Illinois who does not want CPR at home has that choice recorded on a signed IDPH Uniform POLST form (or an older IDPH DNR form that is still valid), kept where EMS can find it.

form.label: IDPH Advance Directives page (Uniform POLST form)

items.title: Use the Michigan do-not-resuscitate order form if it applies
items.done: Done when an adult in Michigan who wants no resuscitation outside a hospital has an order on the statutory form, dated and signed by them or their patient advocate, their attending physician and two witnesses aged 18 or over, at least one of whom is not their spouse, parent, child, grandchild, sibling or heir, and it is kept within reach wherever the person is cared for outside a hospital.

items.title: Record your organ and tissue donation decision in your state's registry
items.done: Done when each adult who chooses to donate is on their state's donor registry and has told their family.

items.title: Join the Illinois organ and tissue donor registry if you choose to donate
items.done: Done when each person who chooses to donate is on the Illinois Secretary of State's organ and tissue donor registry and has told their family.

form.label: Illinois Organ/Tissue Donor Registry (Office of the Secretary of State)

items.title: Join the Michigan Organ Donor Registry if you choose to donate
items.done: Done when each person who chooses to donate is on the Michigan Organ Donor Registry, has the heart symbol on their license or ID, and has told their family.

form.label: Michigan Department of State: organ donor registry
